newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TWAY, BLAKE LEAD BUICK INVITATIONAL AFTER FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TWAY, BLAKE LEAD BUICK INVITATIONAL AFTER FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Bob Tway and Jay Don Blake, two former winners of this event, were atop the leaderboard after the first round of the Buick Invitational Thursday at Torrey Pines.
Tway, who won his first PGA Tour event here in 1986, shot an eight-under par 64 on the North Course. Blake, whose only Tour victory came here in 1991, shot a 65 on the North Course.

Olin Browne and Taylor Smith also shot 65s, though Browne's score came on the more difficult South Course. Dan Forsman, Frank Lickliter and Tom Pernice each shot 66. Lickliter was a last-minute replacement for Dave Rummells, who withdrew.
Mark O'Meara, who won the AT&T Pebble Beach National Pro-Am on Sunday, continued his stellar play with a 67 on the South Course.

"I gave myself a lot of opportunities," said Tway, who has won seven times on the PGA Tour, but just once since 1991. "I was able to capitalise on all of them. The golf course is playing more difficult because of the high rough, but if you keep it on the fairway you'll give yourself a chance to go at it."
Of Tway's eight birdies, only one was longer than 12 feet. He did not make a bogey.
"I came into the year wanting to putt better," he said. "I've always been a good putter, but I didn't spend enough time on it last year."
Blake also played the North Course without making a bogey. He made seven birdies, including four in a five-hole stretch on the front nine.

"You can't ever say it is easy," Blake said. "It felt like I hit a lot of fairways. My main goal was to hit in the fairways. The rough is brutal. You used to be able to kind of bomb it and find it and hope the trees don't get in the way."
